title: Make the ATM network's answers say what really happened

blocks.text: Your server authorizes cash withdrawals for an ATM network, and the network's operations team has sent three complaints this week:

items: During last night's database maintenance every withdrawal was answered `05`, and their on-call engineer was not paged.
Twice an ATM dispensed cash for a withdrawal that your server has no record of. Both times the journal's disk was full.
Since someone's quick fix, withdrawals over the limit come back `96` instead of `61`.

blocks.text: All three pass through `AnswerFailures` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/AnswerFailures.java`, which stands right before `SendResponse`. Its comment lists what the network's specification says. Finish `codeFor` and `needsAnswer`, marked `TODO`. About six lines in total.

The tests deploy a real TransactionManager with Q2, in the test's own JVM. Participants in front of yours report causes, throw, approve, approve part of the amount, or refuse on their own, as each test asks.

cases.says: a failure a participant reported is answered, as a reply to its request, with the network's code for that cause
a thrown exception, or a cause the network's table doesn't list, is answered 96, never with a decline
an approval already in RESPONSE is replaced when a later participant aborts the transaction
a partial approval (10) is an approval too, and is replaced on the abort path
a refusal a participant built itself is the answer and is not replaced, while a failure with nothing built gets one

origin.section: 10.3 On the Abort Path `SendResponse` Sends Whatever `RESPONSE` Holds

concepts: SendResponse sends whatever RESPONSE holds on the abort path, so an approval built before a later failure must be replaced, a refusal kept, and the answering participant must run after every participant that can fail.
Participants report causes in the Result and one abort participant maps them to field 39; a thrown exception or an unlisted cause is 96, never a decline.
